quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What are the penalties for a DUI conviction?
questions.explanation: DUI penalties can include a suspended or revoked license, fines, jail time, and payment for emergency services.

questions.question: In Virginia, what must all passengers under age 18 do?

options.text: Wear a seat belt only in the front seat.
Wear a seat belt only in the back seat.
Wear a seat belt in any seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a seat belt in any seat.
questions.explanation: The driver must make sure all passengers under 18 wear a seat belt or use a child safety seat, no matter where they sit in the car.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to look for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Then quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving into the other lane.

questions.question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even if there's no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: There is a highway entrance ramp ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: A driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that the driver is distracted and unsafe.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because a crash is more likely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Do not go until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop for other drivers or pedestrians. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means you should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes of traffic will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to:

options.text: Pedestrians crossing a street or highway.

questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians at crosswalks and intersections. Also yield to funeral processions and military convoys. Do not cut through or join them.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for other vehicles and pedestrians to pass before going.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and turn around to reach your exit.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and turn around to reach your exit.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how they work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how they work.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where the turn signals, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn are located and how they work. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if you need to.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means slow down as you approach an intersection. Let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can affect your driving ability. These include all types of alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has several curves.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. Safe driving is not possible when you drink alcohol or use other drugs. Impaired driving puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without good tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take steps to drive safely in the dark for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet, 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid on quick turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the more likely you are to die in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic can also be dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes or exit. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Every time you drive, you:
questions.explanation: Every time you drive, you accept responsibility for your actions. You must obey Virginia's traffic laws and keep yourself, your passengers, and others safe on the road.
